reel.caption:
Breaking your FD for a 0.5% higher rate: why can it cost you ₹2,000?

Illustrative ₹2 lakh FD booked at 6.5% for 3 years, broken after 1 year:
Banks pay the rate for the period actually held (say 6%), minus a premature-withdrawal penalty (often 0.5%, up to 1%) = 5.5%. Year-1 interest: ₹11,000 instead of ₹13,000.
Re-invested at 7% for the last 2 years: ₹2,000 more. Net gain ≈ ₹0.
Simple interest, before tax; your bank's card rates and penalty decide the real answer.
